verses.text: After King Ahasuerus's anger cooled, he thought about Vashti, what she had done, and the decree he'd issued against her.
The king's attendants said, "Let a search be made for beautiful young women who have never been with a man.

Appoint officers in every province to gather those young women at the fortress of Susa. Let them stay in the women's quarters under Hegai, the king's eunuch in charge of the women, and give them beauty treatments.
Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in Vashti's place." The king liked the idea and acted on it.
A Jewish man named Mordecai lived in the fortress of Susa. He was the son of Jair, descended from Shimei and Kish, a Benjamite.
His family had been taken from Jerusalem among the exiles deported with King Jeconiah of Judah by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah, also called Esther, because she had no father or mother. She was lovely in form and appearance. When her parents died, Mordecai took her in as his own daughter.
When the king's order was announced, many young women were brought to the fortress of Susa and placed in Hegai's care. Esther was brought into the palace and placed in his care as well.

Hegai liked Esther and treated her kindly. He promptly gave her beauty treatments and her share of food, assigned her seven attendants chosen from the palace, and moved them all to the best part of the women's quarters.
Esther hadn't told anyone who her people or her relatives were, because Mordecai had told her to keep it to herself.
Every day Mordecai walked in front of the courtyard of the women's quarters to find out how Esther was doing and what would happen to her.
Each woman's turn to go to King Ahasuerus came after twelve months of beauty treatments: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetics.
When a young woman went to the king, she could take whatever she wanted from the women's quarters to the royal residence.

She went in the evening and returned the next morning to the second women's quarters, under Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch in charge of the concubines. She could only see the king again if he was pleased with her and called for her by name.

When it was Esther's turn, she asked only for what Hegai, the king's eunuch in charge of the women, recommended. Esther was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle, and Mordecai had adopted her. Everyone who saw her looked on her favorably.
Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal residence in the tenth month, Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

The king loved Esther more than any of the other women and showed her more favor and kindness than any of the other young women. He put the royal crown on her head and made her queen in Vashti's place.
Then the king held a great banquet for his officials and servants in Esther's honor. He declared a holiday throughout the provinces and gave gifts with royal generosity.
When the young women were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
Esther still hadn't disclosed her family or her people. She followed Mordecai's instructions, just as she had when he was raising her.
While Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the entrance, Bigthan and Teresh, became angry and plotted to kill King Ahasuerus.
Mordecai found out about the plot and told Queen Esther. She told the king and gave Mordecai credit for the report.
The matter was investigated and found to be true. Both men were hanged, and the event was recorded in the royal chronicles in the king's presence.
